title: X Minus One
paragraphs: NBC's classic science-fiction anthology adapted stories by major genre writers and presented original scripts about space, aliens, future societies, technology, and the social consequences of scientific change.
Adult science-fiction anthology continuing the creative line of Dimension X.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: NBC original run (April 24, 1955 to January 9, 1958) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] and 1973 experimental revival (January 27, 1973 to January 27, 1973).

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include William Welch (producer and radio adaptor), Fred Collins (announcer), Daniel Sutter (director and transcriber), Ernest Kinoy (radio adaptor and writer), George Lefferts (radio adaptor, writer, and author), Bob Hastings (performer), and Wendell Holmes (performer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]], [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]], and [[org|org.244a08401c2c9142|WRVR-FM]].

The stories often return to space travel and exploration, time travel and temporal displacement, alien life and first contact, human identity and personhood, robots and artificial beings, and computers and artificial intelligence.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Dimension X predecessor and script continuity, Science-fiction magazine adaptation pipeline, Adult science fiction in network radio’s television era, and Old-time-radio nostalgia revival attempt.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|the-chase|The Chase]], [[show|theater-five|Theater Five]], [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], and [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]].
